title: Tenant soft-hibernation & warm-recall PRD (sketch)
content:
Summary:

Quick sketch of a feature we can offer for Dedicated customers who have highly intermittent workloads: soft-hibernation + warm-recall. Goal is a low-cost, predictable way to let tenants reduce active reserved footprint during long idle windows while preserving fast recovery for bursts, and maintaining stronger isolation than pure shared opportunistic bursting. This is NOT another burst-credit system — it’s an operational lifecycle tied to tenant heartbeat signals and warm cache retention profiles.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Many Dedicated customers pay for reserved GPU pools sized for peak traffic that occurs only occasionally (daily/weekly campaigns, batch inference spikes).
- Current options: keep capacity always warm (expensive) or rely on cross-tenant opportunistic bursts (risk noisy neighbors and inconsistent latencies).
- Customers want a contractable mechanism to temporarily scale down paying compute but guarantee recovery latency bounds and isolation behavior during recall.

Primary user outcomes:
- Customer can schedule/automate temporary hibernation windows for predictable cost savings without manual full decommissioning.
- On recall, warm KV caches and minimal orchestration steps restore model serving paths to stable latency within SLA (e.g., p95 <= X ms in Y seconds after recall).
- Platform maintains isolation guarantees: hibernated tenants do not compete for hot-server caches and receive protected preemption lane on warmup nodes.

Key metrics / success criteria:
- Effective cost reduction for tenants during hibernation windows (target 40–70% lower infra charge for those windows).
- Mean time-to-stabilize (MTTS) after recall: target 30–90s depending on model size and recall profile.
- Recall success rate (no timeouts/errors during first N requests) > 99.5%.
- No measurable P95/P99 regression for unaffected tenants (isolation preserved).

High-level approach (concept):
1) Soft-hibernate: customer marks one or more tenant pools as hibernated (via API/Console/Schedule). The control plane:
   - deallocates GPU workers but preserves minimal metadata + persisted KV cache artifacts into a warmstore (S3-like with fast-read/restore semantics).
   - issues tenant-level state change and an optional staggered drain timeline (drain-for: 0..t seconds) to let in-flight work finish.
2) Warm-recall: customer triggers recall (explicit API / scheduled wake / traffic-based heartbeat). The control plane:
   - allocates a small set of warm-recall nodes (pre-warm lane) with affinity for the tenant (soft exclusive).
   - restores KV prefixes & runtime artifacts from warmstore prioritized by recent prompts and model shards.
   - routes first request to recovery lane with augmented retry/backoff (fast failure to fall back to hosted model if configured).
3) Isolation lane (sleepy-shield): during warm-recall, recall lane has preemptive access to networking and kernel reservations so that other opportunistic workloads cannot evict the warm nodes until warm period expires.

Autoscaling integration and policies:
- Soft-hibernation is orthogonal to usual autoscaler but introduces a new state machine: ACTIVE <-> SOFT_HIBERNATED <-> RECALLING.
- Autoscaler rules:
  * If tenant heartbeat absent for X hours, optionally auto-hibernate based on policy and customer consent.
  * Recall operation can request a target concurrency and autoscaler will ensure minimal per-node concurrency to meet latency SLOs.
  * During recall, autoscaler uses a conservative ramp curve (e.g., 1 node -> 3 -> 8) with faster prewarm deadlines if customer has a paid "fast recall" addon.
- Interaction with burst credits: hibernated tenants do not consume global burst credits; recall uses a separate quota bucket (recall-credits) to prioritize resource allocation.

APIs & Console changes (proposal):
- New REST endpoints: /tenants/{id}/hibernation (POST: schedule, GET: status, DELETE: cancel).
- Additional payload fields: retain_cache_profile (none/minimal/full), recall_priority_level (standard/fast/premium), expected_idle_window.
- Console: Hibernation view in Dedicated -> Tenants showing scheduled windows, expected savings estimate, and MTTS history.

Operational & billing model:
- Billing: reduced reserved compute charge while hibernated (e.g., 50% reserved discount) + restore fee when recall happens (covers fast retrieval and prewarm scheduling).
- Optionally: "Commit-lite" contracts where customers accept bounded number of recalls/month at fixed per-recall fee.

Edge cases & failure modes:
- Warmstore latency higher than predicted -> fallback to hosted model or degrade gracefully with client-visible banner.
- Recall partial success (some shards restored, others pending) -> partial degraded latency; platform should route lower-SLA requests to fallback models.
- Network partition between control plane and region -> automatic longer hibernation, alert ops.

Isolation and security considerations:
- Artifacts stored in warmstore must be encrypted with tenant KMS.
- Hibernation state changes logged to audit trail; recall operations emit trace spans for billing reconciliation.
- When tenant is hibernated, background maintenance tasks (profiling, autoscaler signals) should not surface tenant artifacts to other tenants.

Rollout plan / experiment ideas:
- Phase 0: internal alpha with 2 engineering customers; test recall latency for Llama-style and transformerXL-style models.
- Phase 1: opt-in beta for larger set (10 customers) with usage-based pricing; measure MTTS and cost delta.
- Phase 2: GA with tiered recall SLAs (fast/premium/standard) and console controls; add API quotas for recalls.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to quantify and guarantee MTTS for very large 80B models (cold RAM+NVMe restore time) — estimate profiles and possible multi-step recall (networked caching + streaming weights).
- Pricing model: per-hour discount vs per-recall fee mix? run experiment with 3 pilot customers.
- Exact warmstore SLA & replication for multi-region recall.
- Interactions with private deployments (on-prem) — provide an on-prem variant that uses cluster-local warmstore.

Related notes / inspirations:
- Inspired by database hibernation patterns (Aurora cold snapshots) and cloud VM hibernation but tuned to model runtime artifacts and KV caches.
- Different from "ephemeral burst" because soft-hibernate aims to reduce cost for slow seasonal tails rather than handle sudden spikes.

Action items (near term):
- (Grace) draft API spec + example curl payloads (due 2025-06-26).
- (Ravi) prototype warmstore restore/replay for 7B and 70B models (P0).
- (Marisol) design console mockups for schedule view and savings estimator.
- (Ethan) define recall-credit accounting / billing events.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally rough; we want engineering + SRE feedback on the viability of warmstore speeds and autoscaler interactions before polishing into a full PRD.

End of sketch.
